mainTopic: Mixing the blood of the פר and the שעיר on יום כיפור, and whether a bowl inside a bowl or bast inside a bowl counts as a חציצה
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא in which רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן argue about the blood of the פר and the שעיר on יום כיפור. רבי יאשיה says the כהן גדול mixes the two bloods before sprinkling on the golden altar. רבי יונתן says each blood is sprinkled by itself. Each brings a פסוק, and רבי יונתן explains "אחת" as one set from each blood. A second, unnamed ברייתא supports mixing, and the גמרא says it follows רבי יאשיה, just like our משנה. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה's line "he placed the full into the empty." רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא whether a מזרק placed inside another מזרק counts as a חציצה. Proofs from the משנה and from a כהן standing on a friend's foot are both pushed away. In a second version the question is whether this is a proper דרך שירות, and the answer is yes: "two vessels and one service." Finally רמי בר חמא asks about bast (palm fiber) inside the bowl. The proof from a sponge in מי חטאת is rejected because water is thin. In a second version רב חסדא rules that it is כשר with blood, which seeps through, but פסול with a קומץ, which cannot pass through.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: each blood is sprinkled separately
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן disagrees with רבי יאשיה and says the blood of the פר and the blood of the שעיר are each sprinkled on their own, without mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: He sprinkles from this one by itself, and from that one by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא. רבי יאשיה said the bloods are mixed, and now רבי יונתן gives the opposite view: no mixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the sprinklings on the מזבח הזהב (golden altar) on יום כיפור. According to רבי יונתן, the כהן גדול does one full set of sprinklings with the פר's blood, and then a separate full set with the שעיר's blood.

keyTerms.meaning: From this one by itself (each blood alone)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says:
from this one (the bull's blood) by itself,
and from that one (the goat's blood) by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing opinion to רבי יאשיה (earlier) in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bull's blood and the goat's blood are sprinkled separately, not mixed.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה challenges: the verse says 'once'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה attacks רבי יונתן from the word "אחת" (once) in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה said to him: But wasn't it already stated: "Once"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה challenges רבי יונתן with a פסוק that says the atonement on the altar is done "once."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמות ל:י says the כפרה on the golden altar is done "אחת", one time. If each blood is sprinkled separately, the כהן ends up doing two sets of sprinklings. So רבי יאשיה argues the bloods must be mixed, so there is only one set.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it already stated (a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya said to him:
But wasn't it already stated: "Once"!
phrases.notes: שמות ל:י — atonement on the altar's corners once a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יונתן's ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's view that each blood is sprinkled by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says "אחת", only one set; sprinkling separately makes two sets, so the bloods must be mixed.

steps.title: רבי יונתן counters with 'the blood of the bull and the blood of the goat'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן answers back with his own פסוק, which lists each blood separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said to him: But wasn't it already stated: "Of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן fires back with a different פסוק that seems to support his view. This sets up his explanation of "אחת" in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא טז:יח names each blood on its own: "מדם הפר ומדם השעיר". רבי יונתן reads this as teaching that each blood gets its own sprinklings. Now there are two פסוקים pulling in opposite directions, and he must still explain "אחת".

keyTerms.meaning: Of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said to him,
but wasn't it already stated:
"Of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge to רבי יאשיה, answering his פסוק with another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's view that the bloods are mixed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists each blood separately, which suggests each is sprinkled on its own.

steps.title: רבי יונתן explains 'once': one set per blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that "אחת" means one set from each blood, not two sets from the same blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why is "once" stated? To tell you: once and not twice from the bull's blood, once and not twice from the goat's blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן answers רבי יאשיה's challenge by giving the word "אחת" a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה read "אחת" as "one set in total." רבי יונתן reads it as "one set per blood": the כהן may not do two sets from the פר's blood, or two sets from the שעיר's blood. Now both פסוקים fit his view, so the מחלוקת stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, why was it stated?
To tell you (introduces what a פסוק really teaches)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יאשיה: the bloods are mixed, and "אחת" means one set in total. רבי יונתן: separate, and "אחת" means one set from each blood.

phrases.english: If so, why is "once" stated?
To tell you:
once and not twice from the blood of the bull,
once and not twice from the blood of the goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יונתן's reply by neutralizing רבי יאשיה's פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "אחת" means only one set of sprinklings altogether, so the bloods must be mixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: "אחת" means one set from each blood, not two sets from the same blood. This fits sprinkling them separately.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: the bloods should be mixed
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא, with no name attached, derives that the bloods are mixed and proves it from "אחת".
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: "And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat": that they should be mixed together. Do you say mixed together, or perhaps only this by itself and that by itself? The verse states: "Once."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that rules the bloods must be mixed. It uses the same word "אחת" to rule out sprinkling them separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק "ולקח מדם הפר ומדם השעיר" ("he shall take", one taking) is read as teaching mixing. The ברייתא considers the separate option and rejects it because of "אחת". This is רבי יאשיה's reasoning, not רבי יונתן's.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא
Do you say... or perhaps it is only... (a ברייתא testing two readings)

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
"And he shall take of the blood of the bull and of the blood of the goat"
— that they should be mixed together.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: Do you say that they should be mixed together,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִזֶּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: or perhaps it is only from this one by itself
and from that one by itself?
The verse states: "Once."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא on the same question, which sides with mixing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bloods of the פר and the שעיר are mixed together, based on "אחת".

steps.title: The unnamed ברייתא follows רבי יאשיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the unnamed ברייתא as following רבי יאשיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the unattributed ברייתא is in accordance with רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא labels whose view the second ברייתא follows: רבי יאשיה, who holds the bloods are mixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is simply naming whose view the unnamed ברייתא follows. Our משנה also has the כהן mix the bloods, so the משנה, this ברייתא, and רבי יאשיה all agree against רבי יונתן.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and the סתם ברייתא follow רבי יאשיה: the bloods are mixed before sprinkling on the golden altar.

phrases.english: And the unattributed baraita is in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which opinion the ברייתא in step 5 follows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The anonymous ברייתא agrees with רבי יאשיה (mixing), matching the משנה.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: pouring the full bowl into the empty one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about pouring blood from the full bowl into the empty one to mix it well.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He placed the full one into the empty one," etc.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא returns to the next phrase in the משנה to start a new discussion about the bowls (מזרקים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, after mixing, the כהן גדול poured from the full מזרק into the empty one so the bloods would blend well. Mentioning two bowls opens the next question about one bowl placed inside another.

keyTerms.meaning: Etcetera (the rest of the quoted line)

phrases.english: He placed the full one into the empty one, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: quotes the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן pours blood from the full bowl into the empty bowl to mix it.

steps.title: A bowl inside a bowl: does it count as a barrier?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא whether collecting blood in a מזרק placed inside another מזרק is valid, or whether the outer bowl is a חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: If he placed a bowl inside a bowl and collected the blood in it, what is the law? Does an item interpose with its own type, or does it not interpose?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question (בעיא) is asked. If the כהן collects the blood in an inner bowl while holding the outer bowl, is that valid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קבלה (collecting the blood) must be done properly by the כהן with the כלי. Here the outer bowl stands between the כהן and the inner bowl. The question is whether something of the same kind (a bowl with a bowl) counts as a barrier, or whether the two bowls are treated as one.

keyTerms.meaning: A bowl used to collect sacrificial blood
An item with its own type

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the blood touching the outer bowl. The problem is whether the outer bowl blocks the connection between the כהן and the bowl actually receiving the blood.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked of Rav Ḥisda:
If he placed a bowl inside a bowl,
and collected the blood in it, what is the law?
Does a type with its own type interpose,
or does it not interpose?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's mention of two bowls and asks about a bowl inside a bowl.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an object of the same type (a bowl within a bowl) counts as a חציצה, which would make the קבלה of the blood invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of מין במינו and חציצה reaches beyond this case. It decides when an extra layer of the same material breaks a required direct connection.

steps.title: רב חסדא tries to answer from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה already answers the question. 'He placed the full into the empty' seems to mean setting a full מזרק inside an empty one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this. The משנה says, 'He placed the full one into the empty one.' Doesn't that mean he set a full bowl down inside an empty bowl?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רמי בר חמא's question by pointing to a line in our משנה. He reads it as describing one bowl sitting inside another bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן גדול set a full מזרק inside an empty one during the service, then a bowl inside a bowl is not a חציצה. That would make receiving blood this way valid.

keyTerms.meaning: You have learned it (it is already taught)

phrases.english: He said to him: You have learned it:
He placed the full into the empty.
phrases.notes: Quoting the line of the משנה brought in Step 7.

phrases.english: What, is it not

phrases.aramaic: הוֹשִׁיב מִזְרָק מָלֵא לְתוֹךְ מִזְרָק רֵיקָן?
phrases.english: that he set a full bowl inside an empty bowl?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the שאלה of Step 8 using the משנה line from Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That a מזרק inside a מזרק is not a חציצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: נָתַן אֶת הַמָּלֵא בָּרֵיקָן.

steps.title: The משנה means pouring, not setting inside
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא rejects the proof. The משנה means he poured the full bowl into the empty one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means he poured the full bowl into the empty bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא pushes back. He says the משנה is talking about pouring blood from one bowl to the other, not putting one bowl inside the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is only about pouring, it says nothing about a bowl sitting inside a bowl. So the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He poured (emptied one vessel into another)
A bowl used to receive and sprinkle sacrificial blood

phrases.english: No, he poured a full bowl
into an empty bowl.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, עֵירָה מִזְרָק מָלֵא לְתוֹךְ מִזְרָק רֵיקָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה offered in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of the משנה, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'placed the full into the empty' can mean pouring, so it does not prove anything about one bowl sitting inside another.

steps.title: Pouring was already mentioned earlier in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects that the משנה already taught pouring in its first clause, so this line must mean something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה already taught pouring in the first part: 'He poured the blood of the bull into the blood of the goat!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רמי בר חמא's reading. The משנה already said the blood was poured, so why would it say it again?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה does not usually repeat itself for no reason. If pouring was already stated, then 'he placed the full into the empty' should teach something new, like setting one bowl inside another.

keyTerms.meaning: But he (the תנא) already taught it

phrases.english: But the tanna already taught it in the first clause:
He poured the blood of the bull
into the blood of the goat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's reading that the line means pouring.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it means pouring, the line repeats what the רישא already said, which would be pointless.

steps.title: A second pouring to mix the blood well
steps.stepSummary: The second pouring is not extra. It is done to mix the two bloods very well.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is in order to mix them very, very well.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא explains why the משנה mentions pouring again. After the first pouring, the כהן pours back again so the bloods are fully mixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause is the main mixing of דם הפר into דם השעיר. The second line adds another pour back into the empty bowl so the mixing is complete. So the line is not a repeat, and the proof about a bowl inside a bowl is still gone.

phrases.english: In order to mix them very, very well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the repeated phrase its own purpose (a second, thorough mixing).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second pouring is a needless repeat, so the line must mean a bowl inside a bowl.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second pouring has its own purpose, mixing very well, so the משנה does not prove anything about a bowl inside a bowl.

steps.title: Proof from a כהן standing on a vessel or a friend's foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new proof: a כהן standing on a vessel or on his friend's foot is פסול. A foot on a foot counts as a חציצה, so one thing blocks another of the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he was standing on a vessel, or on his friend's foot, his service is disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to answer the question. A כהן must stand right on the floor, and if his friend's foot is under him, that is a block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A foot under a foot is the same kind of thing, yet it still counts as a חציצה. So maybe a bowl under a bowl is also a חציצה, and receiving blood that way would be פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (bringing a source as proof)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he was standing on top of a vessel,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי רֶגֶל חֲבֵירוֹ — פָּסוּל!
phrases.english: or on top of his friend's foot, it is disqualified!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיָה עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבֵּי כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה failed, the גמרא tries a new source for the question of Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That something of the same kind (a vessel under a vessel) still counts as a חציצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a כהן standing on a vessel or on his friend's foot is פסול.

steps.title: A foot is different because it cannot be nullified
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. A friend's foot cannot be canceled out and treated as part of the כהן's own foot, but a vessel can become part of another vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A foot is different, because he cannot nullify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the foot proof. A foot is special, so you cannot learn from it to a bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's foot never 'disappears' into someone else's foot. It always stays a separate thing, so it blocks. An inner bowl can be treated as part of the outer bowl, so it may not block at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullify, cancel out as a separate thing

phrases.english: A foot is different,
because he cannot nullify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רֶגֶל, דְּלָא מָצֵי מְבַטֵּיל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the comparison from a foot to a vessel.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A foot cannot be nullified, but a vessel can be nullified to another vessel, so the cases are not alike.
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, the חציצה question of a מזרק inside a מזרק is not resolved, because both proofs (from the משנה and from the foot case) were pushed away. Steps 15-16 give a second version of the question, and that version is answered.

steps.title: Second version: is this a proper way of doing the service
steps.stepSummary: Some say רמי בר חמא asked something else: is using a bowl inside a bowl a normal way to do the service at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what he asked him: Is this a proper way of service, or is this not a proper way of service?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a different version of רמי בר חמא's original question. It is not about חציצה but about whether this is a respectful, normal way to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the worry is not that the outer bowl blocks the blood. The worry is that using two bowls together may not be a proper דרך שירות, which would make the service פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A proper manner of Temple service

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question asked later. איכא דאמרי means the original question from Step 8 is being retold in a different way, about דרך שירות instead of חציצה.

phrases.english: Some say,
this is what he asked him:
Is this a proper manner of service,
or is this not a proper manner of service?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the version of the question in Step 8 with a different version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether serving with a מזרק inside a מזרק counts as a proper דרך שירות.

steps.title: Two vessels, one service
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל learns from a פסוק that two vessels can be used for one service. So it is a proper way of service.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'All the service vessels with which they serve in the Sanctuary.' This means two vessels and one service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second version of the question with a ברייתא. The פסוק shows that using two vessels together for one service is normal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of vessels (plural) with which they do the service. דבי רבי ישמעאל reads this as two vessels working together in one act of service. So a bowl inside a bowl is a proper דרך שירות.

keyTerms.meaning: The service vessels of the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version (איכא דאמרי), the question is answered: a מזרק inside a מזרק is a proper דרך שירות, based on 'two vessels and one service.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that holding one Temple vessel inside another while serving does not ruin the service in this version. The two vessels are seen as working together.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"All the service vessels
with which they serve in the Sanctuary" (במדבר ד:יב)
two vessels and one service.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, it is a proper דרך שירות, because the פסוק teaches two vessels and one service.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the איכא דאמרי version, using a מזרק inside a מזרק is a valid way of service.

steps.title: Bast inside the bowl: does it block the blood?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא about bast placed inside a מזרק. Does a different kind of object block the blood, or not, since the blood seeps through it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: if a כהן put bast (palm fiber) inside the bowl and caught the blood in it, what is the law? Does a different kind of thing block, or does it not block? Maybe since the blood seeps through, it does not block. Or maybe it makes no difference, and it still blocks.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks a new question. Earlier the question was a bowl inside a bowl. Now it is bast, a fiber, inside a bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the issue was one vessel inside another vessel of the same kind. Here the thing inside is a different kind of material, and it is not a vessel at all. The question has two sides. Maybe the blood passes through the fibers and reaches the bowl, so nothing is really blocked. Or maybe any foreign object in the bowl counts as a חציצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bast, the rough fiber that grows around a palm tree
The bowl used to catch the blood of a קרבן
One kind of thing together with a different kind
Blocks or separates, making a חציצה

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked of Rav Ḥisda:
If he placed bast inside the bowl,
and received the blood in it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The blood passes through the bast into the bowl.

phrases.english: Does a kind with something not of its kind block,
or does it not block?
Since it seeps through, it does not block;
or perhaps it makes no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question about חציצה that follows the bowl-inside-a-bowl discussion. This time the object inside is a different material.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether bast inside a מזרק counts as a חציצה between the blood and the vessel, given that blood seeps through it.

steps.title: Proof from the sponge in the מי חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a proof from a sponge sitting in the water of מי חטאת. The כהן keeps sprinkling until he reaches the sponge, so the sponge does not block the rest of the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: we already learned this. He keeps sprinkling until he reaches the sponge!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to answer the question with a known teaching about sprinkling the מי חטאת of the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case a sponge was inside the container of מי חטאת. The water soaked inside the sponge cannot be used. Even so, the rest of the water can still be sprinkled until the sponge is reached. This shows that a foreign object sitting in the vessel does not block the liquid around it. So bast should not block the blood either.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned it in a משנה
Water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה

phrases.english: He said to him: we have learned:
He sprinkles and keeps going
phrases.notes: This refers to sprinkling מי חטאת from a container that has a sponge in it.

phrases.english: until he reaches the sponge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 17 by comparing it to a known teaching.
steps.raayaObject: A foreign absorbent object inside a vessel does not block the liquid from counting as being in the vessel.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching about מי חטאת: he sprinkles until he reaches the sponge.

steps.title: Water is thin, but blood is thick
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Water is thin and surely passes through a sponge, but thicker blood may not pass through bast.
steps.simpleTranslation: Water is different, because it is thin.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from the sponge is rejected. The two liquids are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if water and blood behave the same way. Water is thin, so it surely flows through the sponge and reaches the vessel. Blood is thicker, so it might not truly seep through the bast. If it does not, the bast could still be a חציצה, so in this version the proof fails. The next step gives another report, in which רב חסדא answers the question directly.

phrases.english: Water is different, for it is thin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the original question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Water is thin and blood is thick, so whether the liquid passes through is not the same in both cases.

steps.title: Second version: blood is valid, a handful of flour is not
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב חסדא answered directly. With blood the service is כשר, because the blood passes through the bast. With a קומץ it is פסול, because the flour cannot pass through.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is how רב חסדא answered him: with blood, it is כשר. With a קומץ, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story. In this version רב חסדא gave a clear answer that splits into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether the item can pass through the bast. Blood is a liquid, so it seeps through and reaches the bowl, and the bast does not block it. A קומץ of a מנחה is solid dough. It sits on top of the bast and never touches the vessel, so the bast blocks it.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a second version of the story)
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה, which must be placed in a כלי שרת

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version the key is whether the item passes through. Blood seeps through the bast, so there is no חציצה and it is כשר. A קומץ cannot pass through, so the bast blocks it and it is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against the sponge proof. It is a different report of what רב חסדא answered in the first place.

phrases.english: Some say:
this is how he resolved it for him:
With blood, it is valid.
With a handful, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version that replaces steps 18-19 with a direct answer from רב חסדא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bast does not block blood, because the blood seeps through, so it is כשר. Bast does block a קומץ, because the flour cannot pass through, so it is פסול.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether bast is a חציצה depends on whether the item can pass through it to reach the vessel.
